items.intro: A policy update changes the probability of an observed action. PPO compares that change with an advantage estimate, and clipping behaves differently for helpful and harmful actions.
items.task: Calculate the negative mean clipped surrogate objective from supplied log probabilities and advantages. Explore both signs of the advantage before interpreting the clipping operation.
requirements: new_logps, old_logps and advantages are nonempty one-dimensional arrays of equal length. Log probabilities must be nonpositive, and abs(new_logps-old_logps) must be at most 60.
Require 0<=clip_ratio<1. Let r=exp(new_logps-old_logps). For each example use min(r*advantage, clip(r,1-clip_ratio,1+clip_ratio)*advantage).

Return the negative mean of those terms as a scalar. This is the forward surrogate loss only; the caller supplies fixed old log probabilities and advantages. There is no value loss, entropy bonus, advantage estimator or training loop.
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Multiply before taking the minimum
hints.body: A negative advantage reverses the ordering of the two ratio-weighted terms.

hints.title: Clipping is not a hard trust-region constraint
hints.body: A ratio outside the interval can still affect the loss. Inspect negative advantages when the ratio is too large.

explanation: For a positive advantage, increasing the action probability beyond the upper clip boundary stops improving this surrogate. For a negative advantage, reducing it below the lower boundary stops improving the surrogate.
The minimum chooses the less optimistic term for either sign. Simply clipping every ratio and then averaging fails on the other side of the interval.
Ported the upstream clipped surrogate to NumPy with bounded log-ratio validation. Autograd detachment and full PPO training are outside this forward-only contract.
